column1: # Shared fork-layer rename table: NeoForge 26.1.2 -> 26.2 (Minecraft 26.2; NeoForge 26.2.0). Applied FIRST (nearest) on the
# 1.21.1 text, then the 26.1.2/1.21.11/... tables on whatever it left -- so a row here is written against the ORIGINAL
# 1.21 spelling, and a row that must beat an older table's rewrite of the same text is a regex (regexes run in table
# order, nearest first, before the type sweep). A rename row reaches the AUTHORS' files only: never an overlay (CATALOG
# §W8) nor a shared helper, so the helpers in shared/26.2/java are written in the 26.2 dialect by hand.
#!exhaustive  # shared library: most forks use only some of these rows
# QUADS, TRIANGLES, TRIANGLE_STRIP, TRIANGLE_FAN, LINES, DEBUG_LINES, DEBUG_LINE_STRIP, POINTS), VertexFormat.IndexType ->
# GlStateManager.SourceFactor / DestFactor (1.21.5+: com.mojang.blaze3d.platform.SourceFactor / DestFactor) are ONE enum,
# com.mojang.blaze3d.platform.BlendFactor, with the same constant names. Every spelling at once: a 1.21.5 row turns the
# GlStateManager form into the platform form, but it runs after this one and would leave a type 26.2 does not have.
# Tesselator is gone: the shared helper keeps 1.21's getInstance().begin(mode, format) over one shared ByteBufferBuilder.
# MultiBufferSource (and its immediate BufferSource) is gone (26.2 records into a StagedVertexBuffer); the shared helper is
# the 1.21 interface drawing at endBatch. Minecraft.renderBuffers().bufferSource() is its main() instance.
# The WHOLE receiver chain is matched (`Minecraft.getInstance().gameRenderer.renderBuffers()`), never its tail.
# Minecraft.getMainRenderTarget() -> GameRenderer.mainRenderTarget(); getMainRenderTarget is a Minecraft method only.
# RenderSystem.getModelViewMatrix() -> getModelViewMatrixCopy() (a Matrix4f copy; the Matrix4fc view is gone).
# GameRenderer.getMainCamera() -> mainCamera(). 1.21.11's rows rewrite .getMainCamera().getYRot() etc. into the record-style
# accessors but run AFTER this table, so the accessor rows are repeated here on the original text (anchored on the bare
# method name, not the dot, so they are not the 1.21.11 rows' patterns).
# Minecraft.setScreen(screen) -> Minecraft.gui.setScreen(screen) (Minecraft keeps only setScreenAndShow). Anchored on the
# receivers that are a Minecraft: Minecraft.getInstance(), and the conventional minecraft / mc / client fields.
# EditBox.setFilter(Predicate) is gone in 26.2 (NeoForge's re-added filter left EditBox); the helper restores it with a
# responder that puts the last accepted value back (CATALOG V100: it takes the responder slot). Only a ONE-argument call
# that is an EditBox's: a lambda or method-reference argument, or a receiver named like a box/field/input -- never
# AbstractTexture.setFilter(blur, mipmap). The receiver is the whole chain (`this.screen.box`), never its tail.
# Font.drawInBatch(...) is gone (world text is a submitText node); the helper draws it into the caller's MultiBufferSource.
# the receiver is the whole chain: `Minecraft.getInstance().font.drawInBatch(` -> `Fonts.drawInBatch(Minecraft.getInstance().font, `
# Shared fork-layer rename table: NeoForge 21.11 -> 26.1.2 (Minecraft 26.1.2; NeoForge 26.1.2). Applied FIRST (nearest) on the
# 1.21.1 text, then the 1.21.11/1.21.10/... tables on whatever it left -- so a row here is written against the ORIGINAL
# 1.21.1 spelling. A rename row reaches the AUTHORS' files only: never an overlay (CATALOG §W8) nor a shared helper, so an
# overlay inherited from a parent target that still has the 1.21.x shape is fixed by hand in targets/26.1.2/java.
#!exhaustive  # shared library: most forks use only some of these rows
# ---- Block light (CATALOG M64): 1.21.2 dropped getLightBlock's BlockGetter/BlockPos and 26.1 renamed it getLightDampening
# (BlockBehaviour and BlockStateBase alike; unchanged through 26.3). An override left as getLightBlock overrides nothing
# and vanilla's default runs (15 for a solid render, else 0 if it propagates skylight, else 1). A body that read the
# dropped level/pos fails to compile, loudly, rather than being guessed at.
# ---- Properties.hasPostProcess(StatePredicate) is postProcess(PostProcess) in 26.1: the hook returns the position to
# post-process after world generation (vanilla's Blocks.postProcessSelf returns pos) or null for none. Only the
# always-true predicate is rewritten; any other predicate is left for the compiler to name.
# Shared fork-layer rename table: NeoForge 21.10 -> 21.11 (Minecraft 1.21.11; NeoForge 21.11). Applied FIRST (nearest) on the
# 1.21.1 text, then the 1.21.10/1.21.8/... tables on whatever it left. 1.21.11 is where the 26.x split starts: Mojang renamed
# ResourceLocation to Identifier here (CATALOG §V4, a pure type rename) and moved ~330 classes (the fork's generated
# moves.generated.tsv carries those; they are derived from the staged jars and are not copied into this library).
# A rename row reaches the AUTHORS' files only. It never reaches an overlay (CATALOG §W8) and never reaches a shared HELPER
# (layer.py copies helpers into the prepared tree AFTER the rename pass), so helpers in shared/1.21.11/java are written
#!exhaustive  # shared library: most forks use only some of these rows
# ---- ResourceLocation -> Identifier, and the members that followed it (each read from the 1.21.11 sources, not guessed)
# FriendlyByteBuf.readResourceLocation()/writeResourceLocation(rl) -> readIdentifier()/writeIdentifier(id). The method names exist on
# FriendlyByteBuf only, so a call-shape row is safe without a receiver.
# ResourceKey.location() -> identifier(). NOT a bare `.location()` row: TagKey.location() is STILL location() in 1.21.11 (a record
# component) and a mod's own records have `location()` accessors too (this fork has two). Anchor on what returns a ResourceKey.
# ---- Camera: getX() -> x() (xRot/yRot/position/blockPosition/entity). Anchored on getMainCamera(), the one receiver whose TYPE is
# certain; a variable named `camera` is a guess (CATALOG X40) and stays a per-file fix.
# ---- RenderType.<factory>(..) -> RenderTypes.<factory>(..). The static factories left RenderType (whose only static is now
# create(name, RenderSetup)) for RenderTypes. ONLY names that exist in 1.21.1 with the same arguments and the same culling:
# entityCutout still culls and entityCutoutNoCull still does not on 1.21.11 (it is 26.2 that swaps them, CATALOG V60). Written
# fully qualified so no import has to be added.
# ---- numeric permission levels (CATALOG V15, the same shape as 26.2): level 2 is Commands.LEVEL_GAMEMASTERS. Fully qualified.
# ---- GeckoLib 4.x text -> 5.4: the baked-model types left cache.object and the built-in layers got a `builtin` package (same
# simple names; diffed from the 5.3-alpha-3 and 5.4.5 jars, each simple name unique on the new side)
# ---- mixin targets (found by tools/audit-mixin-targets.py; javac cannot see them)
# Camera.setup(BlockGetter, Entity, boolean, boolean, float) takes a Level on 1.21.11. A callback that mirrors the vanilla parameter list
# has to follow, or Mixin refuses the descriptor. Fully qualified so no import is needed.
# A mixin DESCRIPTOR names classes with slashes (`Lnet/minecraft/...;`), which neither the dotted moves.generated.tsv rows nor the
# type rows above can reach. The two that matter for a client mod: RenderType moved into `rendertype`, ResourceLocation is Identifier.
# ---- GeckoLib 5.4 controllers (1.21.11): forceAnimationReset() is reset(). The State enum is gone too (a STOPPED check
# is per file, CATALOG M55). ⚠ reset() now sets PlayState.STOP: a STOPPED check AFTER a reset in the same predicate
# reads true at once, where forceAnimationReset() left the state alone -- read the state first.
# The State enum is gone: a STOPPED comparison (4.x getControllerState() or 5.x getAnimationState()) becomes
# net.eca.mv.GeoControllers.isStopped(controller) -- read it before any reset() in the same predicate.
# Shared fork-layer rename table: NeoForge 21.8 -> 21.10 (Minecraft 1.21.10; NeoForge 21.10; FML 10). Applied FIRST (nearest
# target) on the 1.21.1 text, then the 1.21.8/1.21.5/1.21.4/1.21.3 tables on whatever it left, so a row here that rewrites
# something those rows also rewrite has to write the 1.21.10 form itself. Measured against neoforge-21.10.64-sources.jar and
# tools/audit-mixin-targets.py on the first layer-fork port (the mixin audit is what finds these: javac cannot see them).
#!exhaustive  # shared library: most forks use only some of these rows
# LevelRenderer.renderLevel(GraphicsResourceAllocator, DeltaTracker, boolean, Camera, Matrix4f, Matrix4f, GpuBufferSlice, Vector4f, boolean)
# (the 1.21.6-1.21.8 shape) gained a third Matrix4f, the culling projection, after the other two (1.21.9). The 1.21.10 rows write
# the whole descriptor / parameter list from the 1.21.1 text, as the 1.21.8 ones do. Both rows below carry an inert lookbehind (`(?<=/)`, `(?<![\w$])`):
# the table loader refuses two rows with the same `from` (CATALOG X31), and these match exactly what the 1.21.8 rows match; being
# nearer they run first and the 1.21.8 pair never fires on a 1.21.10 build.
# ... and the callback of an @Inject into it (the same eight 1.21.1 parameters, then the CallbackInfo)

re:(?<![\w$])(@Inject\(method = "renderLevel"[\s\S]{0,300}?private void [\w$]+\()DeltaTracker (\w+), boolean (\w+), Camera (\w+),\s*GameRenderer \w+, LightTexture \w+,\s*Matrix4f (\w+), Matrix4f (\w+), CallbackInfo (\w+)\)
column2: \1com.mojang.blaze3d.resource.GraphicsResourceAllocator mv$allocator, DeltaTracker \2, boolean \3, Camera \4,\n            Matrix4f \5, Matrix4f \6, Matrix4f mv$cullMatrix, com.mojang.blaze3d.buffers.GpuBufferSlice mv$fog, org.joml.Vector4f mv$fogColor, boolean mv$sky, CallbackInfo \7)

column1: # ---- harvested from a dependent fork's 1.21.10 (1.21.9 API): Level.isClientSide is a method; FMLEnvironment.dist is
# getDist(); Screen.hasShiftDown moved to the Minecraft instance; GeckoLib 5.3's renderer addRenderLayer is withRenderLayer
# (a mod that already calls the 1.21.1 isClientSide() method must not get a second pair of parentheses)
# Shared fork-layer rename table: NeoForge 1.21.5 -> 1.21.8 (Minecraft 1.21.8; NeoForge 21.8; FML 9). Applied FIRST (nearest
# target) on the 1.21.1 text, then the 1.21.5/1.21.4/1.21.3 tables on whatever it left, so a row here that rewrites
# something those rows also rewrite has to write the 1.21.8 form itself. Measured against neoforge-21.8.54-sources.jar
# on the first layer-fork port (the unattended 1.21.8 loop's residue, which put every one of these in a per-fork overlay).
#!exhaustive  # shared library: most forks use only some of these rows
# ---- FML 9: @EventBusSubscriber has no `bus` any more; the bus follows from the event class (a mod-bus event is
# delivered on the mod bus, anything else on the game bus), so dropping the argument keeps every subscriber where it was.
# ---- mixin targets (invisible to javac; tools/audit-mixin-targets.py checks them against the target's sources)
# LevelRenderer.renderLevel(DeltaTracker, boolean, Camera, GameRenderer, LightTexture, Matrix4f, Matrix4f) became
# (GraphicsResourceAllocator, DeltaTracker, boolean, Camera, Matrix4f, Matrix4f, GpuBufferSlice, Vector4f, boolean): the
# GameRenderer and LightTexture are gone, and the fog buffer, the fog colour and a "render the sky" flag arrived.
# This row runs on the 1.21.1 text, before the 1.21.4/1.21.3 rows, so it writes the whole 1.21.8 descriptor itself.
# ... and the callback of an @Inject into it (the same eight 1.21.1 parameters, then the CallbackInfo)

re:(@Inject\(method = "renderLevel"[\s\S]{0,300}?private void [\w$]+\()DeltaTracker (\w+), boolean (\w+), Camera (\w+),\s*GameRenderer \w+, LightTexture \w+,\s*Matrix4f (\w+), Matrix4f (\w+), CallbackInfo (\w+)\)
column2: \1com.mojang.blaze3d.resource.GraphicsResourceAllocator mv$allocator, DeltaTracker \2, boolean \3, Camera \4,\n            Matrix4f \5, Matrix4f \6, com.mojang.blaze3d.buffers.GpuBufferSlice mv$fog, org.joml.Vector4f mv$fogColor, boolean mv$sky, CallbackInfo \7)

column1: # Entity.addAdditionalSaveData / readAdditionalSaveData (and LivingEntity's) take a ValueOutput / ValueInput (1.21.6). A handler
# that only PUTS scalars keeps its body (ValueOutput has putInt/putString/putBoolean/...); one that reads needs
# ValueInput's Optional/`...Or` getters and has no contains() -- see the fork's overlay of it for the shape.
# ---- CATALOG V81: the 3-argument playBidirectional / commonBidirectional / configurationBidirectional(type, codec, handler)
# registers only the SERVER handler on NeoForge 21.8 (the 4-argument form takes the client one, @Nullable), and the client then
# refuses to load: "Some clientbound payloads are missing client-side handlers". 1.21.1's 3-argument form served both
# directions, and a handler for a bidirectional payload already branches on ctx.flow(), so passing the SAME handler twice
# restores that exactly. The rows fire only on the 3-argument shape (a 4-argument call has a second top-level comma before its
# closing paren, which the handler group cannot cross). Two rows: a method reference (the usual shape), and an EXPRESSION lambda
# (the text is repeated; a block lambda is not handled -- write that one by hand, or hoist it to a method).
# PacketDistributor.sendToServer moved to the client-only ClientPacketDistributor (NeoForge 21.6+); written fully qualified (a row cannot add an import).
# ---- a former @OnlyIn(CLIENT) method in a common class is verified on the server once strip_onlyin removes the
# annotation; widening a client local to its common type loads the client class there (ClientRefs explains). Only the
# widening assignment form is rewritten: a local that keeps LocalPlayer/ClientLevel needs the client class anyway.
# ---- 1.21.6: Screen.renderWithTooltip draws the background (renderBackground) BEFORE calling render, and Screen.render no
# longer does. A screen whose render() opens with its own renderBackground(...) call (the 1.20.2-1.21.5 idiom) now draws
# it twice, and for a plain Screen the second menu blur throws "IllegalStateException: Can only blur once per frame" --
# a real-client crash the moment the screen opens. Drop the leading call; the background is still drawn once, below.
# Only in a Screen: the match starts at an `extends ...Screen` and takes the first render(GuiGraphics, ...) after it, so a
# widget or other Renderable's render() in a file with no Screen class is left alone.
# Shared rows for a fork layer's 1.21.5 target (and every later one that inherits it).
# 1.21.5 is where CompoundTag/ListTag getters started returning Optional -- the same change 26.2 carries
# ⚠ NOT copied verbatim: the 26.2 rows matched `.getInt(<anything without a comma>)`, which also rewrites a
# ByteBuffer read (`bytes.getInt(at)` -> `bytes.getIntOr(at, 0)`) -- Battle of Lord had no binary readers, the
# first fork that went through here (a Blender/glTF loader) has eight. A shared row cannot know the receiver's
# type, so it anchors on what the NBT API guarantees and a byte offset never is: a string literal key, or an
# UPPER_CASE constant (bare or Class.CONST). A key held in a variable, and a ListTag index, are left to the
# fork's own rows or its workers.
#!exhaustive  # shared library: most forks use only some of these rows
# GameRules.getBoolean/getInt(GameRules.Key) still return the value on 1.21.5 and take an UPPER_CASE key too: a call
# on getGameRules() or with a GameRules.RULE_* argument is not an NBT read (CATALOG M74)
# CompoundTag.getUUID/putUUID/hasUUID are gone; a UUID goes through UUIDUtil.CODEC (the same int[4] on disk).
# Each needs an argument, so the many no-arg Entity.getUUID() calls are untouched.
# CompoundTag.contains(key, type) lost its type argument (from the 26.2 table, verbatim: anchored on a tag id).
# ---- the RenderPipeline rewrite: immediate-mode GL on LegacyGl, 1.21.4 RenderType.create on LegacyRenderType
# (the rest of the layer is java/Legacy*.java, ShaderInstance, ShaderShard, Uniform, RawGlTexture)
# DynamicTexture(NativeImage) gained a name supplier (debug label only)
# ---- Entity.moveTo(...) is snapTo(...) (CATALOG §V39: same body; NOT absSnapTo). A receiver that is a PathNavigation
# keeps its own moveTo(x, y, z, speed) -- X7b: this guesses at the receiver's spelling, it cannot see its type.
# ---- chunk tickets lost their value type: addRegionTicket(type, pos, radius, value) -> addTicketWithRadius(type, pos, radius)
# (the value only told two tickets of one type apart; vanilla 1.21.5 keeps one ticket per type, pos and level)
# ---- SavedData is a SavedDataType (id + constructor + codec) now; Factory is gone, and save() overrides nothing.
# The helper keeps the mod's own save(CompoundTag, Provider)/load(CompoundTag[, Provider]) and the on-disk layout.
# ---- Screenshot.takeScreenshot(target) is callback-based now (the GL backend completes it before returning)
# are sprite()/vertices()/direction()/tintIndex()/shade()/lightEmission(). Anchored on the receiver names a quad is
# conventionally held in (X7b: a guess at spelling, not at type; getSprite() alone belongs to far too many classes).
# ---- RenderTarget is textures, not a framebuffer: frameBufferId / bindWrite(viewport) ask the backend for the FBO
# the receiver is the whole chain (`Minecraft.getInstance().getMainRenderTarget()`), never its tail
# GlStateManager no longer tracks the clear colour; the GL call is the same
# ---- Inventory.items is private in 1.21.5; the same NonNullList is getNonEquipmentItems()
# ---- GeckoLib: its only 1.21.5 line is 5.x. These classes only MOVED from 4.x (the predicate's AnimationState<T> is
# AnimationTest<T> now; 5.x's own processing.AnimationState is a different class). The render-state rewrite itself
# (GeoEntityRenderer<T, R extends EntityRenderState & GeoRenderState>, layers' addRenderData/addPerBoneRender,
# BlockAndItemGeoLayer.getRelevantBones) is per file: CATALOG M49.
# ---- GeckoLib 5 resource ids: a model/animation id is the BARE name under geckolib/{models,animations}/ (tools/fork-port.py
# setup copies the 4.x geo/ and animations/ files there). The 4.x file-path ids do not survive every 5.x line's lookup:
# 5.1-5.3 strip only geckolib/... and the suffix ("geo/x.geo.json" asks for "geo/x"), and 5.4.5's animation lookup strips
# "animations/" and ".json" but not ".animation" (asks for "x.animation") -- so write the bare name everywhere.
# Shared fork-layer rename table: NeoForge 1.21.3 -> 1.21.4 (Minecraft 1.21.4; NeoForge 21.4). Applied AFTER the
# fork's own rows and on top of the 1.21.3 table (a 1.21.4 target inherits 1.21.3). Measured against
# neoforge-21.4.158-sources.jar on the first layer-fork port. CATALOG §M / minor-version-deltas L8+.
#!exhaustive  shared table: most rows are for API this mod does not use
# ---- client reload listeners: a named graph in 1.21.4
# ---- NeoForge 21.4: ClientLevel.partEntities (id -> part map) is gone; dragonParts() is the list of all parts
# ---- TextureManager.register(String prefix, texture) -> named registration (the first argument is a string)
# ---- FML 6 (NeoForge 21.4) early display: SimpleBufferBuilder takes a name for its buffer
# ---- LevelRenderer.renderLevel lost its LightTexture argument (1.21.4); this row runs before the 1.21.3 one, on the
# 1.21.1 text, so it writes the full 1.21.4 descriptor itself
# ---- mixin targets: ScreenEffectRenderer.renderScreenEffect(Minecraft, PoseStack) gained a MultiBufferSource
# (measured on neoforge-21.4.158); an @Inject handler needs the extra parameter before its CallbackInfo
# ---- RenderType.entityTranslucentCull is gone (1.21.2) and RenderType.entityTranslucent sets NO_CULL, so mapping one to
# the other draws the model double-sided (compile-clean, gates green). NeoForgeRenderTypes.getItemLayeredTranslucent is
# the 1.21.1 state: entity-translucent shader, default CULL, translucent, lightmap, overlay, sorted -- same signature on
# 1.21.5 and 1.21.8 (NeoForgeRenderPipelines.ENTITY_TRANSLUCENT_CULL). Rows do not reach overlays. CATALOG M73.
# Shared fork-layer rename table: NeoForge 1.21.1 -> 1.21.3 (Minecraft 1.21.2 API; NeoForge 21.3).
# Harvested from the first layer-fork port and measured against neoforge-21.3.97-sources.jar.
# Every fork that adds a 1.21.3 target inherits these rows (make-fork-layer.py sync-shared copies them to
# .multiversion/shared/1.21.3/, with net.eca.mv = the fork's helper package). Fork-specific rows stay in
# .multiversion/targets/1.21.3/renames.tsv. CATALOG §M (M26-M45) has the reasoning for each row.
# Most of a shared table matches nothing in any one mod, so it is exempt from the dead-rule report as one
# block (CATALOG X23); the fork's own table is checked.
#!exhaustive  shared table: most rows are for API this mod does not use
# the receiver is the whole chain (`this.entity`, `a.b()`), never its tail; a bare super./this. receiver is left alone
# 1.21.2 dropped the yaw argument of EntityRenderDispatcher.render(entity, x, y, z, yaw, partialTick, ...)
# NativeImage: 1.21.1 getPixelRGBA/setPixelRGBA took ABGR; 1.21.2 getPixel/setPixel take ARGB. Convert at the call.
# ---- shaders: the mod keeps building its own ShaderInstances (1.21.1 API) on 1.21.2 CompiledShaderPrograms
# a shard over a VANILLA core shader names its CoreShaders key (M71); written fully qualified, so the helper row below
# does not take it again (it would wrap a ShaderProgram as a Supplier). These must stay ABOVE that row.
# the same through a holder (`ModEntities.X.get().create(level)`), which the bare receiver above cannot see
# ---- registry ids in Properties (CATALOG R25; 1.21.2): a registration supplier names what it builds, and every
# Properties a Block or Item is built from takes that name (net.eca.mv.RegIds). Prefix-only on the supplier, so no row
# has to find a closing parenthesis. A registration by constructor reference (`REG.register("name", Y::new)`, Y a Supplier-shaped no-arg
# constructor) becomes the same entering supplier; without it Y builds its Properties with no name recorded
# the same, written fully qualified (the bare rows above cannot see past the package prefix)
# ---- mixin targets (invisible to javac; audit-mixin-targets.py checks them against the target's sources)
# EnderDragon.hurt(List<Entity>) (the head/body contact damage) became hurt(ServerLevel, List<Entity>) in 1.21.2
# @Accessor returning Ingredient no longer matches the field (callers then fail to compile and get .orElse(null))
# GeckoLib 4.7.3 (1.21.3) / 4.8.5 (1.21.4): GeoRenderLayer preRender/render gained a trailing int colour
# ---- entities: Entity.hurt is `final void` since 1.21.2 (M66). A BOOLEAN use of it (`if (x.hurt(..))`, `b = x.hurt(..)`,
# `&& x.hurt(..)`, a lambda's value) is hurtServer's result through the helper -- never a "did health drop?" comparison,
# which miscounts an absorbed, blocked or cancelled hit. A statement call stays (it still compiles); a capitalised receiver
# (a static `Api.hurt(e, s, a)`) and `super.` are left alone.
# an Entity.hurt OVERRIDE is a hurtServer override (the server is the only side 1.21.2 calls it on)
# Mob.doHurtTarget and MobEffect.applyEffectTick take the ServerLevel (1.21.2)
# Recipe.canCraftInDimensions and Entity.getBoundingBoxForCulling are no longer overridable: keep the method, drop @Override
# ---- items: InteractionResultHolder is gone; an item's use returns an InteractionResult. A success or consume carrying a
# stack keeps it (heldItemTransformedTo; for the held stack itself that is the plain result)
# ItemCooldowns is keyed by stack (its cooldown group) since 1.21.2
# Ingredient.of(ItemStack...) is gone; an ingredient of one stack's item is Ingredient.of(item)
# GeckoLib 4.7+ (4.7.3 on 1.21.3, 4.8.5 on 1.21.4): GeoModel's resource getters and GeoRenderLayer.getDefaultBakedModel
# take the renderer; GeoEntityRenderer.getDeathMaxRotation takes the partial tick (a GeckoLib 5 GeoRenderState getter is left)
# ---- items whose 1.21.1 getDefaultAttributeModifiers override no longer runs (M68): its `super` base is the item's own
# ATTRIBUTE_MODIFIERS component, and the stack form is applied by the AttributeOverrides helper (named in a comment so
# ---- blocks: light queries lost their BlockGetter/BlockPos; neighborChanged takes the redstone Orientation; the
re:(void neighborChanged\(BlockState \w+, Level \w+, BlockPos \w+, Block \w+), BlockPos (\w+), boolean (\w+)\)
# ---- client: GuiGraphics.blit takes the render type first also when the texture is built in place; the profiler is per
# thread (Minecraft/Level.getProfiler() are gone) -- the whole receiver chain goes
